Subject: Hosting preference and residency constraints — next steps

Hi Oliver — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on hosting/residency: 

- FinBridge priority: EU-only data residency for any customer data and model context. APAC is a future requirement (H2 pilot).
- Primary use case: low-latency payments fraud scoring (short text inputs, 150 token avg).
- Preferred outcome: minimal operational lift but strict residency + auditability.

Options we discussed: Hosted API (fast onboarding, but needs EU region availability and clear cross-border routing rules), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools in EU with predictable throughput), Private VPC/on-prem (full control, longer lead time).

Proposed next steps:
1) We confirm whether FinBridge will accept Redwood Hosted in EU regions (we can pin to eu-west-1) with contractual residency guarantees, or if Procurement requires Dedicated/Private.
2) Ben to share an operations-side matrix comparing latency, TCO estimate, and typical lead times for Dedicated vs Private.
3) If Procurement needs a demo of Private VPC, schedule a technical walkthrough with FinBridge infra (Aisha to own).

Can you confirm procurement's must-haves (e.g., audit log retention window, KMS requirement) so we can route the right collateral? I copied our solutions lead and sales engineer for quick follow-up.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from Procurement & Infosec: 

- Residency: EU-only for all customer PII and model prompt/response context. No outbound routing to non-EU without explicit consent.
- KMS: We use a corporate HSM and want BYOK support (we prefer integrations with Azure Key Vault or AWS KMS).
- Audit: 2 years of immutable audit logs, SOC 2 evidence required.
- SLA: 99.9% preferred for production fraud scoring; we can accept a phased rollout.

Procurement is open to Hosted if Redwood can provide region guarantees + BYOK + the audit retention policy. If not, Dedicated in our EU tenant or Private VPC will be the fallback.

Also: latency budget is 150ms p50 for the inference path; can you confirm if Dedicated vs Hosted will meet that in eu-west-1?

Oliver
Head of Platform Engineering
FinBridge

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Hosting preference and residency constraints — next steps

Oliver — quick technical clarity and a short matrix attached. High-level: 

- Hosted (EU region):
  * Residency: We can pin traffic to eu-west-1 and enforce routing policies. For contractual residency guarantees we offer data locality addendum (we'll provide a draft).
  * BYOK: Supported via customer-managed KMS in Dedicated and Private; Hosted supports BYOK through a delegated KMS model in certain enterprise tiers — we can confirm feasibility for FinBridge with our security team.
  * Latency: For short inputs, Hosted in eu-west-1 typically hits ~90–130ms p50 in our benchmarks.

- Dedicated (Reserved capacity in your EU tenant or Redwood-hosted EU pool):
  * Residency: Full isolation; easier to guarantee audit boundaries.
  * BYOK: Native support.
  * Latency: Slightly better p50 (70–110ms) due to pinned capacity and placement control.
  * Lead time: 4–8 weeks depending on capacity commitment and procurement.

- Private VPC / On-prem:
  * Residency: Full control, meets strictest compliance.
  * BYOK: Native/HSM support.
  * Lead time: 8–16 weeks; requires network setup and possibly an on-site appliance for air-gapped setups.

I attached a short PDF (deployment-options-summary.pdf) and an EU residency checklist (eu-residency-checklist.xlsx) with the specifics Procurement usually asks for. If Procurement can accept Hosted with BYOK and our data locality addendum, that will give you the fastest path to prod.

-Ben
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
